description:
## Problem
The bundled TPC-DS 4.0.0 `dsdgen` writes corrupt item keys into the web-channel refresh data. Root cause, confirmed in the public tpcds-kit source (`tools/s_web_order_lineitem.c`, `mk_s_web_order_lineitem`):

```c
if (++nItemIndex  > nItemCount)
   nItemIndex += 1;
```
When the per-order item cursor passes the end of the item permutation, it keeps counting instead of wrapping, so `getPermutationEntry` reads past the end of `pItemPermutation` (undefined behaviour). `s_catalog_order_lineitem.c` wraps correctly (`nItemIndex = 1`). At SF 1, refresh sets 1 and 2 (seed 20260709) contain one web order (152 in set 1) whose lines 2-12 take out-of-range entries: macOS reads item 1 for all of them (10 duplicate (order, item) pairs, which the web_sales primary key forbids); Linux reads garbage keys such as `AAAAAAAACICICICI` that match no item, and two web returns point at them. Catalog and store refresh files are byte-identical across platforms. SF 0.01 is not affected.

Consequences: on Linux every engine enforcing NOT NULL fails TPC-DS maintenance step LF_WR (CedarDB nightly 44568679855 and 44832232783; reproduced with DuckDB on Linux), ClickHouse Local silently stores default keys, and refresh data differs between operating systems.

## Fix
Change the branch to `nItemIndex = 1;` (verified on a tpcds-kit 2.10 build: duplicates drop from 10 to 0 at SF 1 set 1, and only the 11 affected lineitems and 2 returns change). Patch file and evidence: `/tmp/tpcdskit/web-lineitem-item-wrap.patch` (to be committed as `_sources/tpc-ds/web-lineitem-item-wrap.patch` with a `_sources/tpc-ds/PATCHES.md` entry).

## Decision gate
The 4.0.0 tools sources (`_sources/tpc-ds/tools/*.c`) are gitignored under the TPC EULA and not present on this machine. Owner supplies them (or confirms where they are) before the rebuild. Then: apply the patch, rebuild all six platforms with `_sources/compilation/scripts/compile-all-platforms.sh`, commit `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-ds/*`.

## Guardrails
- Patch only the wrap branch; no other generator change. Base data (non-refresh) must stay byte-identical: compare a full SF 1 base generation before and after on one platform.
- No BenchBox-side filtering or repair of refresh rows.
- Rebuild every shipped platform in one change, so no platform keeps the corrupt binary.

## Verification rubric
Pass only if: a regression test generates SF 1 refresh sets 1 and 2 with the bundled dsdgen and asserts no duplicate (order, item) pair in `s_web_order_lineitem` and every web return's (order, line) matches a lineitem with the same item; macOS and Linux refresh files are byte-identical for SF 1 set 1 (seed 20260709); base data unchanged; and a nightly `fullspec-cedardb` run passes LF_WR.
